key_insight: Assimilate sparse flow observations in the clean-state space with an explicit observation-error covariance via an ensemble Kalman update, making diffusion-based data assimilation more Bayesian and principled.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more physically grounded path to reconstruct turbulent flow states from limited sensors, potentially reducing reliance on expensive adjoint-based variational methods or heavy ensemble simulations.
method: Use a generative diffusion model to represent the flow-state prior.
Assimilate observations in the denoised clean-state space instead of directly tuning likelihood weights.
Apply the prescribed observation-error covariance through an ensemble Kalman update to balance prior and data.
evidence_signal: In Lorenz-63, the method achieved lower trajectory error and equation residual than other diffusion-based posterior sampling methods, and in 2D Rayleigh-Bénard convection it matched DNS statistics at large scales.
watch_item: The reported ensemble underestimates posterior uncertainty, so uncertainty calibration may need improvement before robust deployment.
paper_title: Toward Principled Generative Data Assimilation of Turbulent Flows from Sparse Observations
